subsystems.name: Quantum transducer
subsystems.role: the element whose quantum state shifts measurably when a tiny magnetic or electric field changes — the actual sensor.
parts: laser-cooled atomic vapour in a cell

subsystems.name: Control and excitation
subsystems.role: prepares the quantum state and reads out its shift.

subsystems.name: Magnetic shielding and field control
subsystems.role: keeps the Earth's field and building noise from swamping the signal.

subsystems.name: Optical readout
subsystems.role: converts faint fluorescence or microwave transmission into a digital signal.

subsystems.name: Clinical interface
subsystems.role: puts the sensor next to the body in a usable, tolerable way.

subsystems.name: Software and inference
subsystems.role: separates the biological signal from noise and turns it into a clinical reading.

buildSteps.title: Make the sensing material
buildSteps.detail: For diamond sensors, high-purity diamond is grown by chemical vapour deposition and doped so that nitrogen-vacancy centres sit at controlled depths and orientations.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the sensor element
buildSteps.detail: The diamond is cut, polished and patterned with microwave antennas and optical structures; vapour cells are instead filled with an alkali metal and a buffer gas and sealed.

buildSteps.title: Assemble control optics
buildSteps.detail: Lasers, modulators, fibres and microwave electronics are aligned so each sensor can be addressed individually.

buildSteps.title: Shield the instrument
buildSteps.detail: Layers of high-permeability metal plus cancellation coils reduce ambient fields by many orders of magnitude.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate against a known field
buildSteps.detail: Each sensor is characterised for sensitivity, bandwidth and drift using reference magnetic fields, often traceable to a standards laboratory.

buildSteps.title: Build the array
buildSteps.detail: Many sensors are tiled into a wearable or probe array, with wiring and heat managed so it can touch a patient.

buildSteps.title: Reconstruct an image or reading
buildSteps.detail: Algorithms combine the array's signals into a magnetic map of a brain, heart or tissue sample.

buildSteps.title: Validate clinically
buildSteps.detail: The device is compared against existing scanners on real patient cohorts before any diagnostic claim is made.

prerequisites.tech: High-purity diamond growth and defect engineering
prerequisites.why: the sensitivity of a diamond sensor depends on placing single defects precisely, which is still hard at wafer scale.

prerequisites.tech: Compact narrow-linewidth lasers and microwave electronics
prerequisites.why: they prepare and read the quantum state, and their noise floor sets the device's limit.

prerequisites.tech: Effective magnetic shielding and active field cancellation
prerequisites.why: biomagnetic signals are a billionth of the Earth's field, so shielding is what makes them visible.

prerequisites.tech: Robust analysis for very weak biosignals
prerequisites.why: separating a real biomarker from environmental and physiological noise is the practical bottleneck.
no quantum sensing device has yet been cleared as a stand-alone diagnostic for cancer or neurology.

pathway.milestone: optically pumped magnetometers and SQUID arrays record brain and heart fields in research labs, and diamond magnetometers detect single magnetic nanoparticles in samples
pathway.unlocks: non-invasive functional measurement without cryogenic cooling, and laboratory-scale molecular detection.

pathway.milestone: wearable, room-temperature brain scanners in clinical pilot studies
pathway.unlocks: presurgical mapping and epilepsy assessment in ordinary hospital rooms rather than shielded suites.

pathway.milestone: quantum sensors as contrast detectors for hyperpolarised MRI and magnetic nanoparticle labelling
pathway.unlocks: earlier detection of small tumours and mapping of molecular targets.

pathway.milestone: validated, regulated diagnostic instruments incorporating quantum sensors
pathway.unlocks: routine early diagnosis of cancer and neurological disease at the point of care.
